title: Repeated-grip trial-order contrast fails to improve cross-cohort HbA1c prediction beyond maximum strength
abstract: Averages and maxima discard the ordering of repeated physiological measurements. We tested a bilateral normalized third-minus-first grip contrast as a predictor of concurrent HbA1c beyond maximum grip, age, body size, creatinine, hemoglobin and demographics. A frozen sex-specific spline ridge model trained in NHANES 2011–2012 (n=3913) transferred to separately recruited NHANES 2013–2014 (n=4414). Adding the contrast increased examination-weighted MSE from 0.73455 to 0.73764 percentage-points squared; difference +0.00309, joint source/target PSU-bootstrap 95% interval [-0.00085, +0.03549]. The registered improvement criterion failed, as did all sensitivity point comparisons. This exploratory negative result does not establish equivalence or absence of metabolic information in repeated grip. Same-program cohort transfer is not independent-program validation.
